The original idea with far fewer, far larger dots, and the fade starting at 36%. Seven countable columns rather than a gradient.
A pixel dissolve. Hard edges survive scaling in a way soft ones never do, and squares read as data rather than as decay.
Vertical bars thinning to nothing. The simplest dissolve there is, and the likeliest to still work at 29 px.
The dissolve follows gills radiating from the stem, so it is the same mushroom losing its gills rather than an arbitrary left-to-right fade. Joins this idea to the other one you liked.
Three flat zones: solid, half, sparse. No gradient anywhere, and the most mechanically robust of the eight.
Solid, and then the shape persists only as a dashed line. The most elegant and the most fragile.
Horizontal strips of decreasing length — a mushroom coming apart line by line, like a print that only half developed.

Cap and stem solid, the base coming apart. The uncertainty is where it really is — the base is where the volva is, and the part most people leave in the ground. The falling dots read as spores, which was an accident and is worth keeping.
